beats.text: A man, maybe 40s, with a nervous tic spends the afternoon with the giant rhubarb-like leaves, round burrs, first-year = leaf rosette with no stalk — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.

Everett leans in, voice low. "Here's what we figured out about a line of ducks, walking in perfect formation. In the dark. That is not normal duck behavior.. Break the line. The line is one animal, but only while it's whole. Strike a duck that ISN'T the head and the line splits — both halves hunt on their own and the formation dies. Break the line, then thin the pieces."

🔥 The fire settles. Pavel has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Night Court — I put it down today." "No sound. That is the warning. The moon-shadow on the ground is growing — and there is no sound at all. Owls don't make sound when they hunt." "It missed — and it is already turning. The second dive re-aims at where you moved." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Jesse says "Did it look at you? Before?" Elijah says quietly "And you're still standing." Someo
